site.name: Ascension Mine
site.location: Ralston Buttes Mining District near Tucker Gulch, Jefferson County
overview: Ascension Mine, also recorded as the Nair Prospect and Nare Lease, was a small uranium producer in Jefferson County's Ralston Buttes district. The mine was discovered in 1955 and produced intermittently from 1956 through 1972.

timeline.title: Discovery
timeline.description: The mineralized vein was discovered in place, and the site entered federal mineral records as the Ascension Mine.

timeline.title: Production begins
timeline.description: Recorded uranium production began in 1956; the documented ore grade was approximately 0.23 percent U3O8.

timeline.title: Intermittent district production
timeline.description: USGS district records identify the Ascension Mine as contributing production during 1960 through 1963.

timeline.title: Last recorded production
timeline.description: The final documented production year was 1972, when Cotter Corporation was listed as the owner.

moreHistory: The mine exploited a uranium-bearing vein in the Ralston Buttes district. Federal records list uranium as the primary commodity, with copper and lead also present.

USGS Professional Paper 520 includes a geologic map and sections for the Ascension Mine area. Later mineral study of a historic Ascension sample identified quartz, uraninite, pyrite, and possible thorianite.

The mapped point lies near Tucker Gulch and represents the documented mine site. Historical mine ground can be unstable or contaminated, and this record does not establish public access or safe entry.
